title: Grateful Dead Live at Electric Theater on 1969-04-26
lineage: Panasonic SV-3700 > Cardas cable S/PDIF > Edirol UA-5 > USB > WaveLab Mastering: In WaveLab with Nomad Factory Plugins > CD Wave > TLH > Flac
source: Soundboard Cassette x 1 > DAT; Encore Source: 7 inch Master Reels @ 7.5ips 1/2trk > DAT

ai_review.summary: A solid 1969 soundboard capture with Jerry and Phil front‑and‑center, featuring a smoking Viola > Caution Jam > Viola sequence and plenty of early‑Dead fire.
ai_review.review: The recording is a well‑preserved 1969 soundboard mix that, while not flawless, presents the band clearly with Jerry Garcia and Phil Lesh prominently in the front. The show itself is high‑energy, highlighted by a blazing Viola > Caution Jam > Viola stretch, fiery Cryptical > Other One passages and standout early gems like Silver Threads and It's Sin.

ai_rating.rationale: All six reviews are overwhelmingly positive (average 4.8★), emphasizing strong musical performance and a good‑enough soundboard recording; minor mix quirks keep the rating just shy of perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally solid 1969 board with clear articulation; Jerry and Phil are forward in the mix, Bob and Pigpen sit lower; occasional very quiet passages noted but overall clean for its era.

standout_songs: Cryptical Envelopment > The Other One > Eleven Jam > The Other One
show_quality.setlist_flow: A long, well‑balanced night that builds from a solid first set (Dupree's Diamond Blues) into a second‑set firestorm; transitions flow naturally and the band maintains high momentum throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Front‑and‑center in the mix, delivering a smoking lead on Viola and driving the overall intensity.
band_member_comments.Phil: Prominent bass work, especially powerful during the Viola > Caution Jam segment; described as "absolutely kill[ing] it".
band_member_comments.Bob: Low in the mix but contributes notable banter with Pigpen about drum monitors.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann is up front and solid, providing a strong rhythmic foundation.
